---
title: "Forecast Evaluation Report"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
    toc_float: true
    theme: flatly
    highlight: tango
    df_print: paged
    number_sections: false
params:
  implementation.model.file: NA
  evaluation.model.file: NA
  disease: NA
  name: NA
  email: NA
  reason: NA
  base.box: NA
  general.model.type: NA
  outcome.data.label: NA
  outcome.data: NA
  outcome.name: NA
  training.data.file: NA
  training.variable.name: NA
  training_data_source: NA
  model.descriptions: NA
  variables.crosswalk.file: NA
  location.crosswalk: NA
  state.context: NA
  population.label: NA
  output.dir: NA
  plot.styles: NA
  eval.config: NA
  plot.export: NA
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

```{r loading-parameter-checks}
config <<- forecastEvalReport:::validate_report_params(params)
```

```{r loading-plot-styles, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Resolving plot styles --------------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: If plot_styles were passed through params (injected by generate_      #
# report()), use them. Otherwise fall back to package defaults. This makes     #
# the styles available to all downstream plotting chunks as PLOT_STYLES,       #
# matching the name the plotting functions expect.                             #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ##############################################################
  # Pulling the plot styles file: Using the user provided file #
  ##############################################################
  PLOT_STYLES <- if(!is.null(params$plot.styles) && is.list(params$plot.styles)){
    
    # Calling the user provided file 
    params$plot.styles
    
  ############################################################
  # Creating the plot style file: Using the package defaults #
  ############################################################
  }else{
    
    # Creating the default file
    forecastEvalReport::create_plot_styles()
    
  }

```

```{r loading-eval-config, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Resolving the evaluation config ----------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: If eval.config was passed through params (injected by generate_       #
# report()), use it. Otherwise fall back to package defaults. Makes the        #
# evaluation tuning settings available downstream as EVAL_CONFIG.              #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  #############################################
  # Pulling the user provided evaluation file #
  #############################################
  EVAL_CONFIG <<- if(!is.null(params$eval.config) && is.list(params$eval.config)){
    
    # User provided file
    params$eval.config
    
  #######################################
  # Pulling the default evaluation file #
  #######################################
  }else{forecastEvalReport::create_evaluation_config()}

```

```{r loading-scripts, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Loading CSS and JS files -----------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: Loads all CSS and JS files bundled with the package into the report.  #
# Files are located via system.file() so paths resolve correctly regardless    #
# of where the package is installed. CSS files control the report appearance   #
# and accordion styling. JS files control the floating legend behavior, plot   #
# max phase tracking, legend checkbox sync, and geography dropdown sync.       #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ##############################
  # Loading the main CSS file  #
  ##############################
  htmltools::tags$style(
    paste(readLines(
      system.file("reports", "styles.css", package = "forecastEvalReport")
    ), collapse = "\n")
  )

  ################################
  # Loading the accordion CSS    #
  ################################
  htmltools::tags$style(
    paste(readLines(
      system.file("reports", "accordion.css", package = "forecastEvalReport")
    ), collapse = "\n")
  )

  ############################
  # Loading the max-phase JS #
  ############################
  htmltools::includeScript(
    system.file("reports", "plot-max-phase.js", package = "forecastEvalReport")
  )

  ##################################
  # Loading the floating legend JS #
  ##################################
  htmltools::includeScript(
    system.file("reports", "float-legend.js", package = "forecastEvalReport")
  )

  ###################################
  # Loading the legend checkbox JS  #
  ###################################
  htmltools::includeScript(
    system.file("reports", "syncLegendCheckboxesOnRender.js",
                package = "forecastEvalReport")
  )

  #############################
  # Loading the geo-sync JS   #
  #############################
  htmltools::includeScript(
    system.file("reports", "sync-geo-dropdowns.js",
                package = "forecastEvalReport")
  )

  # NOTE: plotly_fullscreen.js is intentionally NOT loaded here via
  # includeScript(). It is a bare `function(el, x){...}` meant to be attached
  # per-plot through htmlwidgets::onRender() inside build_fullscreen_button().
  # Loading it as a standalone <script> injects a nameless top-level function,
  # which throws "Function statements require a function name" and halts all
  # subsequent page scripts (including the fullscreen + resize logic).

```

```{r loading-implementation-model, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Loading and validating the implementation model file -------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: This section loads and validates the implementation model file        #
# supplied by the user. Validation is dispatched based on the `reason`         #
# (FluSight, COVIDHub, etc.) and aborts the report if the file fails the       #
# format spec. The evaluation model file is loaded and validated separately    #
# in a later chunk.                                                            #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ###################################
  # Loading the implementation file #
  ###################################
  if(!is.na(config$implementation_model_file)){

    implementation_model <<- switch(config$reason,
                        
      ##################                                       
      # FluSight Check #
      ##################
      "FluSight" = forecastEvalReport::validate_flusight_model(config$implementation_model_file),
      
      ######################
      # COVID-19 Hub Check #
      ######################
      "COVIDHub" = forecastEvalReport::validate_covidhub_model(config$implementation_model_file),
      
      #################
      # RSV Hub Check #
      #################
      "RSVHub" = forecastEvalReport::validate_rsvhub_model(config$implementation_model_file),
      
      ###################
      # Metrocast Check #
      ###################
      "MetroCast" = forecastEvalReport::validate_metrocast_model(config$implementation_model_file),
      
      #################################
      # General Model Check: Software #
      #################################
      "Software"  = forecastEvalReport::validate_general_model(config$implementation_model_file,
                                                               state_context = config$state_context),
      
      #################################
      # General Model Check: Internal #
      #################################
      "Internal"  = forecastEvalReport::validate_general_model(config$implementation_model_file,
                                                               state_context = config$state_context),
      
      # Fallback for hubs we haven't implemented validators for yet
      utils::read.csv(
        config$implementation_model_file,
        colClasses     = c(location = "character"),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )

  ##################################################
  # Running if no implementation model is provided #
  ##################################################
  }else{implementation_model <- NULL}

```

```{r loading-evaluation-model, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Loading and validating the evaluation model file -----------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: This section loads and validates the evaluation model file supplied   #
# by the user. The evaluation file is always in the general format regardless  #
# of the operational hub `reason`. Only historical rows are accepted; users    #
# must filter their file to target_end_date < reference_date before passing    #
# it to this validator.                                                        #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ###############################
  # Loading the evaluation file #
  ###############################
  if(!is.na(config$evaluation_model_file)){

    # Validating the evaluation model structure 
    evaluation_model <<- forecastEvalReport::validate_eval_model(
      config$evaluation_model_file,
      state_context = config$state_context
    )

  ############################################
  # Running if no evaluation file is present #
  ############################################
  }else{evaluation_model <- NULL}

```

```{r validating-aux-file, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Validating the auxiliary information cross walk ------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: This section validates the auxiliary information cross walk file      #
# created in a previous step. The goal of this is to ensure that all entries   #
# needed for plotting, definitions, and other pieces of the report are         #
# readily available. Prior to running this, the user must run the function to  #
# build the cross walk. The resulting file path must be provided in the        #
# options file to create the report.                                           #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ####################################################
  # Running if the cross walk file has been provided #
  ####################################################
  if(!is.na(config$variables_crosswalk_file)){
  
    # Reading in the cross walk file 
    variables_crosswalk_raw <<- utils::read.csv(
      config$variables_crosswalk_file,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      na.strings       = c("NA", "")
    )
  
    # Validating the cross walk file 
    variables_crosswalk <<- forecastEvalReport::validate_variables_crosswalk(
      variables_crosswalk_raw,
      verbose = TRUE
    )
  
  ##########################################################
  # Not running if a validation file has not been provided #
  ##########################################################
  }else{variables_crosswalk <- NULL}

```

```{r extracting-implementation-data, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Extracting implementation model metadata -------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: Extracts reference dates, outcome labels, spatial scale, locations,   #
# and projection periods from the validated implementation model. Location     #
# codes are normalized to human-readable names. Results live in `impl_meta`.   #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  #####################################################
  # Triggering if an implementation model is provided #
  #####################################################
  if(!is.null(implementation_model)){

    # Extracting information from the implementation model 
    impl_meta <<- forecastEvalReport::extract_implementation_data(
      implementation_model = implementation_model,
      config               = config,
      save_data            = !is.list(params$plot.export)
    )

  ######################################################
  # Returning NULL if no implementation model provided #
  ######################################################
  }else{impl_meta <- NULL}

```

```{r extracting-evaluation-data, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Extracting evaluation model metadata -----------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: Extracts reference dates, outcome labels, spatial scale, locations,   #
# and projection periods from the validated evaluation model. Location         #
# codes are normalized to human-readable names. Results live in `eval_meta`.   #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------# 

  #################################################
  # Triggering if an evaluation model is provided #
  #################################################
  if(!is.null(evaluation_model)){
    
    # Extracting information from the evaluation model 
    eval_meta <<- forecastEvalReport::extract_evaluation_data(
      evaluation_model = evaluation_model,
      config           = config,
      impl_meta        = impl_meta
    )
    
  #####################################################
  # Returning NULL if no evaluation model is provided #
  #####################################################
  }else{eval_meta <- NULL}

```

```{r assembling-report-data, include=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Assembling the master data set -----------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: Reads outcome and auxiliary variable files, normalizes locations,     #
# filters to forecast locations, and stacks into a single long-format master   #
# data frame saved to the Data/ folder. Result is the path to the saved CSV.   #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  #############################################
  # Runs if the master cross walk is provided #
  #############################################
  if(!is.null(variables_crosswalk)){

    # Calling the assemble report data function 
    master_result <<- forecastEvalReport:::assemble_report_data(
      config               = config,
      variables_crosswalk  = variables_crosswalk,
      impl_meta            = impl_meta,
      eval_meta            = eval_meta,
      implementation_model = implementation_model,
      evaluation_model     = evaluation_model
    )
    
    # Unpack the result: Data frame used downstream
    master_data <<- master_result$data
    
    # Unpack the result: Path saved for reference
    master_data_path <- master_result$path

  ##################################################
  # Returning nothing if no cross walk is provided #
  ##################################################
  }else{master_data      <- NULL
        master_data_path <- NA_character_}

```

```{r forecast-plots, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Building the primary forecast figure -----------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: This section builds an interactive Plotly-based forecast              #
# visualization for each location in the forecast file. Each plot shows the    #
# target data (truth line), implementation model projections and prediction    #
# intervals, historical estimates (when available), evaluation model traces    #
# (per horizon), auxiliary variable traces, modeling period phase ribbons, a   #
# current-week reference line, and a range slider.                             #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Plot-only export request -----------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: When the report params carry a plot.export list, this branch builds   #
# and writes the forecast plot(s) and exits the render early, so none of the   #
# later report sections run. Without it, the report renders normally below.    #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  if(is.list(params$plot.export)){

    # Unpacking the export request from the report params
    .exp     <- params$plot.export

    # HTML keeps the page interactive; any other format is a static image
    .is_html <- identical(.exp$format, "html")

    # Output extension follows the format ("html" or the static type)
    .ext     <- if(.is_html) "html" else .exp$format

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Single-section writer --------------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: One writer call for either output. HTML keeps the interactive page;   #
# any static format screenshots the same section as an image.                  #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

    .write_one <- function(.sec, .file){

      # HTML: write the interactive page
      if(.is_html){
        forecastEvalReport:::write_forecast_html(
          section   = .sec,
          file      = .file,
          overwrite = .exp$overwrite
        )

      # Static: screenshot the same section to an image
      }else{
        forecastEvalReport:::write_forecast_image(
          section   = .sec,
          file      = .file,
          format    = .exp$format,
          width     = .exp$width,
          height    = .exp$height,
          scale     = .exp$scale,
          delay     = .exp$delay,
          font_size = .exp$font_size,
          legend    = .exp$legend,
          overwrite = .exp$overwrite
        )
      }
    }

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Per-location section builder -------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: Builds one section for a location, dispatching on the export target:  #
# the forecast-consistency section when plot = "consistency", otherwise the    #
# forecast section. A static export drops the range slider and forces all data #
# visible via for_export; HTML stays interactive.                              #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

    .build <- function(.loc){

      # Forecast-consistency export: build that section for this location
      if(identical(.exp$plot, "consistency")){
        return(forecastEvalReport:::section_forecast_consistency(
          impl_meta            = impl_meta,
          eval_meta            = eval_meta,
          config               = config,
          implementation_model = implementation_model,
          master_data          = master_data,
          variables_crosswalk  = variables_crosswalk,
          plot_styles          = PLOT_STYLES,
          max_forecasts        = .exp$n_forecasts,
          forecast_every       = .exp$forecast_every,
          end_cushion          = .exp$end_cushion,
          for_export           = !.is_html,
          location             = .loc,
          font_size            = .exp$font_size,
          tick_size            = .exp$tick_size,
          forecast_size        = .exp$forecast_size,
          forecast_color       = .exp$forecast_color,
          observed_size        = .exp$observed_size,
          observed_color       = .exp$observed_color,
          aux_size             = .exp$aux_size,
          aux_color            = .exp$aux_color,
          title_gap            = .exp$title_gap,
          view_start           = .exp$view_start,
          view_end             = .exp$view_end
        ))
      }

      # Forecast plot (default): build the forecast section for this location
      forecastEvalReport:::section_forecast_plots(
        impl_meta            = impl_meta,
        eval_meta            = eval_meta,
        config               = config,
        implementation_model = implementation_model,
        master_data          = master_data,
        variables_crosswalk  = variables_crosswalk,
        plot_styles          = PLOT_STYLES,
        location             = .loc,
        for_export           = !.is_html,
        font_size            = .exp$font_size,
        view_start           = .exp$view_start,
        view_end             = .exp$view_end
      )
    }

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Resolving the output target --------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: A directory target (no extension, a trailing slash, or an existing    #
# directory) writes one file per geography; a single file path writes only     #
# the requested geography, or all of them behind a dropdown.                   #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

    # Directory target: no extension, trailing slash, or existing directory
    .dir_target <- is.null(.exp$file) || dir.exists(.exp$file) ||
      grepl("[/\\\\]$", .exp$file) ||
      identical(tools::file_ext(.exp$file), "")

    ######################################################
    # Per-geography files: directory target, no location #
    ######################################################
    if(is.null(.exp$location) && isTRUE(.dir_target)){

      # Geographies, sourced exactly as section_forecast_plots() does
      .meta <- if(!is.null(impl_meta)) impl_meta else eval_meta
      .geos <- if(!is.null(.meta$locations) && length(.meta$locations) > 0){
        .meta$locations
      }else{
        unique(master_data$location)
      }

      # Resolving (and creating) the output directory
      .dir <- if(is.null(.exp$file)) "." else .exp$file
      if(!dir.exists(.dir)){
        dir.create(.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
      }

      # File stem follows the plot target
      .stem <- if(identical(.exp$plot, "consistency")){
        "forecast_consistency_"
      }else{
        "forecast_plot_"
      }

      # Writing one file per geography
      saved_plot_paths <- character(0)
      for(.g in .geos){

        # Filesystem-safe geography name for the file stem
        .safe <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", .g))

        # Build and write this geography's plot
        .out  <- .write_one(
          .build(.g),
          file.path(.dir, paste0(.stem, .safe, ".", .ext))
        )

        # Collecting the written path
        saved_plot_paths <- c(saved_plot_paths, .out)
      }

    #############################################################
    # Single file: all geographies (dropdown), or the given one #
    #############################################################
    }else{

      # One file: the given location, or every geography in a dropdown
      saved_plot_paths <- .write_one(.build(.exp$location), .exp$file)

    }

    # Stopping the render here so no later report sections run
    knitr::knit_exit()

  }

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Normal in-report rendering ---------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: When no export was requested, render the forecast section into the    #
# report as usual.                                #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  # Render the forecast section into the report
  forecastEvalReport:::section_forecast_plots(
    impl_meta            = impl_meta,
    eval_meta            = eval_meta,
    config               = config,
    implementation_model = implementation_model,
    master_data          = master_data,
    variables_crosswalk  = variables_crosswalk,
    plot_styles          = PLOT_STYLES
  )
```

```{r testing-evaluation, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Testing-period evaluation data and metrics -----------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: This chunk builds the data sets containing the various testing        #
# period metrics, such as percent agreement, forecast bias, peak timing and    #
# magnitude, and the traditional methods. It also takes in the configuration   #
# file, allowing users to set their own thresholds for the metrics.            #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ##########################################################
  # Preparing the testing data and running all the metrics #
  ##########################################################
  testing_eval <<- forecastEvalReport:::build_testing_evaluation(
      eval_meta               = eval_meta,
      master_data             = master_data,
      non_transmission_months = EVAL_CONFIG$non_transmission_months,
      season_start_day_month  = EVAL_CONFIG$season_start_day_month,
      peak_window             = EVAL_CONFIG$peak_window,
      stable_threshold        = EVAL_CONFIG$stable_threshold,
      pct_error_cushion       = EVAL_CONFIG$pct_error_cushion,
      timing_tol_steps        = EVAL_CONFIG$timing_tol_steps,
      mag_tol                 = EVAL_CONFIG$mag_tol
    )

  ##############################################
  # Unpack for the downstream display sections #
  ##############################################

  # Testing data
  data.for.evaluation   <- testing_eval$data

  # Percent agreement table
  percentAgreement.data <- testing_eval$percentAgreement
  
  # Forecast bias table 
  forecastBias.data     <- testing_eval$forecastBias
  
  # Peak timing and magnitude 
  peakPhase.data        <- testing_eval$peakPhase
  
  # Traditional methods 
  traditional.data      <- testing_eval$traditional
  
```

# About: This section produces the orienting paragraph and the per-metric      #
# descriptions shown at the top of the testing-period evaluation section:      #
# percent agreement, forecast bias, peak-phase timing, peak-phase magnitude,   #
# and the traditional (statistical) scoring metrics. The testing-phase date    #
# span is taken from `eval_meta$testing_start` / `eval_meta$testing_end`. When #  
# no testing data is present, the function renders nothing so the section      #
# disappears from the report entirely.                                         #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  ################################################
  # Creating the testing period evaluation intro #
  ################################################
  forecastEvalReport:::section_testing_intro(eval_meta = eval_meta)

# Building forecast bias section -----------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# About: This section builds the interactive Plotly forecast bias figure for a #
# single location, with a Bias (%) / Raw Counts toggle. The figure overlays    #  
# observed-count bars, one dashed line per forecast horizon, and an overall    #
# median line, and shades each non-transmission (No Evaluation) span with      #
# dotted boundaries and a centered label. Row-level values on non-transmission #  
# dates are retained for visual continuity but broken out of the lines with an #  
# all-NA scaffold so the series do not connect across them.                    #
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

  )
